findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed that PIC’s allergen certification is expired. PIC was aware that certification is expired, and will schedule to renew. Ensure compliance by next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed raw chicken stored above raw beef in the walk-in cooler and prep cooler. These storage order violations were also observed in the previous spot check and last routine inspection. Informed PIC that raw beef must be stored above raw chicken due to the beef’s lower minimum cooking temperature. All storage order violations were corrected on site. A spot check will be conducted in the near future to ensure storage order guidelines are being followed. Ensure staff are educated on the proper order of storage for raw meats.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Repeat 
Observed multiple items to be missing date marking (deli meats in prep cooler, cut vegetables and cooked meat in walk-in cooler). PIC was informed that any time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food stored in refrigeration for more than 24 hours needs to be properly date-marked and discarded after 7 days of retention. PIC placed labels on all required foods in prep cooler and walk-in during spot check. A follow-up will be conducted in 10 days (3/12/2025) to ensure that proper date marking is being followed.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:

The green beans were transferred to an appropriate vessel (metal pan) to complete its cooking. Violation is considered corrected on site.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an individual fail to use a barrier to turn off hand-sink faucet. Advised PIC to review proper handwashing with staff. A barrier must be used to turn off the faucet to prevent cross-contamination prior to handling food.

(C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Observed the following storage order violations:
1. Cooked turkey stored under raw beef in walk-in cooler
2. Cooked noodles stored under raw beef in walk-in cooler
3. Fish stored under raw chicken and raw beef in prep cooler
4. Raw hamburger stored over ready-to-eat feta cheese in prep cooler

The inspector will spot check for storage order during the scheduled follow-up.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed containers of cooked chicken and cooked meatloaf in walk-in-cooler to not have a date mark. Per PIC, items were prepared the previous day (6/19/24). Items were marked with proper date during inspection. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. 

Containers of rice, cooked pasta in water and pancake batter are observed on shelves in the walk in cooler without covers. PIC instructed to ensure that all foods are protected from potential contamination while in storage. Lids were supplied to correct.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

The magnetic knife rack to the right of the prep cooler is observed heavily soiled. PIC instructed to clean often enough to protect the food contact surfaces of the utensils attached to it.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing. 

The shelves in the walk in cooler are observed soiled with thick accumulations of dust and rust. PIC instructed to clean them and maintain them clean. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

Multiple shelves in the walk in cooler next to the door to the walk in freezer are observed with rust. PIC instructed maintain smooth and easily cleanable. Painting the wire framing was suggested.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. The can opener blade and ice machine drop guard are not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely so that soil does not accumulate. Blade was cleaned during the inspection to correct. 


4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. The nozzles on the fountain drink machine are observed with a thick accumulation of slime. Situation was discussed with servers. One stated that the nozzles are cleaned every night. Another stated once a week. Inspector suggested that they are removed from the machine, disassembled and cleaned/ sanitized nightly so as to maintain clean. The nozzles were cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment: 3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.  Both chicken and fish are observed in a sink in the kitchen area thawing without an approved method. Discussed with the PIC and instructed them to thaw in an approved method.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment: 6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. Multiple (approximately 5-6) flies are observed in the dish area of the facility. Another pair of flies were observed by the fountain drink machine in the server area. PIC is instructed to contact pest control and ensure effective methods are being used to combat pests in the facility.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Shelves found to be soiled in the walk in cooler of the establishment. Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B). Clean and maintain clean.
